title: The Whole Letters
premise: Beatrix Dravenmoor, a widowed father running Hollowmere's only bookshop, has spent seven years keeping his heart on a strict ration: work, daughter, survival, nothing more. When the town library's anonymous pen-pal program pairs him with an unknown correspondent whose letters slowly undo him, he discovers the writer is Odette Calloway — the developer's daughter buying up the street that will demolish his shop. Torn between the loyalty he owes his late wife's memory and the truth of what he feels, Beatrix must choose between exposing Odette's father's corrupt land scheme and protecting the woman behind the letters; in the end he risks everything at the council vote, and they build something whole where the bookshop stood.
about_author: Tamsin Iversen is a former small-town librarian who writes love stories about stubborn people and the letters they should have sent sooner. She lives above a bookshop not unlike Beatrix's, with a cat named Postscript.

chapters.title: The Rationed Heart
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Morning routine in Dravenmoor Books with his daughter Wren, establishing his philosophy: the heart is a muscle to be trained, contained. He posts flyers for the library's anonymous winter pen-pal program, half-mocking it. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as order.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. New in town under her father's development company, she signs up for the pen-pal program on impulse, wanting one honest connection untainted by her surname. Her first letter is reckless and funny. Emotional beat: loneliness inside privilege.

chapters.title: The First Reply
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The library matches them anonymously; Beatrix writes back dryly, expecting nothing. Their letters spark — she teases, he parries. Neither knows the other's face. Emotional beat: reluctant delight.

chapters.title: Demolition Notices
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Calloway Development posts plans to raze the market street for a retail complex; his lease is doomed. At the public meeting he clashes publicly with Odette, not knowing she is his correspondent. Emotional beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: Ink Against Concrete
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. She reads her pen-pal's furious letter about the demolition and realizes, sickened, that her correspondent is the bookseller from the meeting. She keeps writing anyway, hiding her identity. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren's Map
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Wren, eight years old and sharp, draws a map of 'places worth saving' for a school project — the bookshop at its center. Beatrix begins cataloguing what he'd lose. Emotional beat: fear given a shape.

chapters.title: Letters We Keep
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The correspondence deepens; they exchange secrets neither tells anyone else — his wife's death, her mother's estrangement. Beatrix admits he's falling for someone he's never seen. Emotional beat: intimacy without witness.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Auditing her father's files, she finds falsified environmental surveys buried to fast-track the demolition. She photographs them and says nothing yet. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Coffee, Almost
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. His correspondent proposes meeting; panic wins and he deflects, terrified of ruining the one honest thing he has. Meanwhile Odette visits the bookshop incognito and buys a novel he recommends by hand. Emotional beat: near-miss ache.

chapters.title: Father's Daughter
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Her father announces accelerated timelines and pressures her to charm the council. She sees how he bends people, including her. Emotional beat: complicity curdling.

chapters.title: What Wren Knows
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Wren finds one of the letters and reads it aloud, delighted: 'Whoever this is loves you, Dad.' Beatrix confiscates it and lies about why he can't meet her. Emotional beat: tenderness weaponized against himself.

chapters.title: The Survey Photographs
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. She confronts her father privately; he dismisses her, then threatens to cut her off entirely. She copies the files onto a drive and hesitates over sending them to her pen-pal. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Snowfall Deadline
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Final eviction notice arrives; the council vote is set for midwinter. He writes his pen-pal that he may be gone before they ever meet. Emotional beat: grief preemptively rehearsed.

chapters.title: Anonymous No More
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. She mails the evidence drive to the library's pen-pal address with no note but her initials. Beatrix receives it, recognizes the handwriting from the letters, and connects it to the woman from the meeting. Emotional beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: Enemy, Correspondent
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Fury and longing collide as he rereads every letter searching for lies and finds only truths he can't forgive yet. Wren asks why he looks like someone died. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Her father offers her the project lead if she discredits the survey leak; instead she goes to the bookshop and confesses everything to Beatrix's face. He turns her away. Emotional beat: courage met with a closed door.

chapters.title: Pieces vs. Whole
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He rereads his late wife's last letter and finally hears what it said: don't lend pieces, risk the whole. He drafts a reply to Odette he never sends, then decides to deliver it in person. Emotional beat: thaw.

chapters.title: Council Eve
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the night before the vote, Beatrix and Odette meet in the closed library among the returned pen-pal letters. Truths laid bare; not forgiveness, but alliance. They plan to present the evidence together. Emotional beat: wary partnership kindling.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, climax. Before the council, Odette testifies against her own father with the falsified surveys; Beatrix speaks for the street, for Wren's map. The project stalls pending investigation. Her father disowns her publicly. Emotional beat: the whole heart, wagered and held.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Fallout: her name is mud in town, her money gone, her father facing inquiry. Beatrix finds her packing a bag to leave and stops her — not with a speech, but by reading her own first letter aloud. Emotional beat: chosen belonging.

chapters.title: Spring Inventory
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Months later: the investigation saves the street, the bookshop endures, and Odette works the counter beside him while Wren teaches her the register. The heart, he concedes, was never containable after all. Emotional beat: earned domestic joy.

chapters.title: The Whole Letters
chapters.summary: Dual POV, coda. They bind every letter they exchanged into a single volume for the library's shelf, first page to last, enemies-to-strangers-to-lovers in their own hands. Wren adds a final page of her own. Emotional beat: the story kept, the heart whole.
